chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who passed the time when people enter the state of Ihram, but he forgot or was unaware, so he did not enter Ihram until he arrived in Mecca. He feared that if he returned to the time/place, he would miss the Hajj. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should exit the Haram (sanctuary), enter Ihram, and that will suffice him.'

key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: The designated time/place (Miqat) for entering Ihram
key_terms.يُجْزِئُهُ: It suffices him / is accepted as valid
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: To enter the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who misses the Miqat for Ihram and fears missing Hajj by returning?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) provides a pragmatic concession for the pilgrim who, due to forgetfulness or ignorance, enters Mecca without Ihram, ruling that exiting the Haram boundary to assume Ihram suffices, thereby preventing the loss of the Hajj obligation. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of ease (taysir) in ritual purity and state, ensuring that unintentional errors do not invalidate the core pillar of Hajj.
